newsitem.title: USA: U.S. CASH SOYMEAL- SOME SOYMEAL BASIS OFFERS LOWER.
newsitem.headline: U.S. CASH SOYMEAL- SOME SOYMEAL BASIS OFFERS LOWER.

text.p: Some basis offers for soymeal were lower Thursday on ample supplies and mediocre demand from end users, dealers said.
"The basis is falling to its death," said one Minnesota dealer. "Everybody seems to have meal and beans at the moment."
Trade estimates for the National Oilseed Processors Association varied widely. Trade sources expect the weekly crush to fall between 22.0 to 24.2 million bushels.
That figure compares with last week's crush of 23.577 million. NOPA will report the crush at 0730 CDT Friday.
Dealers who said the crush would climb above last week's pace cited good crushing margins and heavy old crop soybean sales.
"It seems like beans kind of got moving last week," said one broker in the Southeast. "People have beans and they're going to crush them."
Trade sources who saw the crush falling lowered their estimates because more processors are taking downtime for maintenance, they said.
"My guess is lower after just checking the number of people taking downtime," said one Indiana merchandiser.
